title: Law to ban personalized surveillance-based pricing
summary: This bill would prohibit any seller, whether online or offline, from charging different prices to different customers based on personal data collected through cameras, device tracking or other surveillance technology. It includes exceptions for insurance and credit products, loyalty programs and discounts for groups like students, seniors or low-income consumers. Violations would carry civil penalties from $150 for a first offense up to $1,000 for a third or later offense, and the law would take effect 120 days after enactment.
